messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated latency detected for streaming endpoints (region: us-west1). Metric: model-stream-prod p95 jumped from ~220ms -> ~1.1s, p99 from ~800ms -> ~3.2s over the last 2m. Root cause signal: kv-cache eviction spike and prefill/decode imbalance. Incident ID: <https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-032>
ash: Oncall (ash) here — I'm looking. Are customers impacted or just internal SLO alerts?
ravi: Seeing increased client retries, a couple of error reports from one paying customer on streaming timeouts. Telemetry: stream stall observed around token 30-50, then decode waits increase.
ash: Ok. Quick checks: cache hit rate? eviction rate?
jonathan: eviction rate for kv-cache shards 7-12 jumped from 4/s -> 48/s. Prefill write queue backed up, decode workers starved. Looks like slab fragmentation — small keys are getting evicted more often.
lucy: p95 across routes: streaming-chat-api 1.05s, text-generate (non-stream) p95 380ms. So streaming is hit worst.
ash: Priorities: (1) reduce customer-facing impact; (2) stabilize caches to stop tail stalls; (3) investigate root cause. Quick mitigation ideas: throttle prefill concurrency, temporarily route heavy streaming traffic to smaller model variant, bump kv slab allocation for hot shards. Any objections?
ravi: Agreed. I'll throttle prefill via feature flag to 0.4x concurrency. Command: `curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood/internal/flags/prefill_concurrency -d '{"factor":0.4}'` (will take effect in ~15s).
jonathan: I can trigger model routing to fallback-compact for non-enterprise routes: `routectl set model-route streaming-prod --fallback fallback-compact --percent 30` — will reduce strain. Doing it now.
ash: Do it, but keep enterprise customers pinned. Add note to console.
(30s later)
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Feature flag update applied by ravi. prefill_concurrency=0.4.
ravi: Telemetry after throttle: prefill queue length down ~60%, eviction rate down to ~12/s. p95 improved to ~520ms. Still high p99 ~1.9s.
jonathan: Rolled out 30% traffic to fallback-compact. Early signal: CPU/GPU per-shard load dropped ~25% on overloaded hosts. Streaming stalls reduced but not gone.
lucy: We should also consider increasing kv slab for shards 9-12 which show highest fragmentation. Can we do non-disruptive slab bump?
ash: Infra risk? If that requires restart, prefer avoiding for now. Is there a quicker eviction policy change?
jonathan: We can flip `aggressive_hot_eviction` to true on those shards to prefer evicting large cold entries and keep hot prefixes. Command: `redwood-cache admin set --shard 9-12 --policy aggressive_hot_eviction=true` — applies without restart. I'll apply to shard 9 and 10 first.
(another 45s)
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: `aggressive_hot_eviction` enabled on shards 9,10 by jonathan.
ravi: After policy flip: eviction rate normalized ~6/s, cache hit for hot prefixes up ~18%. p95 now ~330ms, p99 ~1.2s. Customer retries decreased.
ash: Good. Next: longer-term followups — need to run a slab defragment job and add prefill vs decode telemetry per-customer to detect imbalance. Also add an automated fallback to smaller model when stream token latency > 800ms for 30s.
lucy: Noted. I'll create a short postmortem and track runbook updates. Immediate ask: oncall handoff in 30m — I'll leave handoff notes here.
ash: Handoff to jonathan at 15:30 UTC. Key items: incident id INC-2026-032, throttled prefill flag, 30% fallback route, aggressive_hot_eviction on shards 9/10, slab defrag scheduled (non-urgent). If p99 doesn't trend down under 1s by handoff, escalate to infra for slab resize.
jonathan: Acknowledged. I'll monitor for next 30m. If anything regresses, @ravi pls be ready to increase fallback to 50%.
ravi: Got it.
incident-bot: :pager: PagerDuty notified for INC-2026-032 (sev: high).
ash: Thanks everyone. Leaving summary in incident doc and will add TL;DR to #status-updates. (reacts :thumbsup:)
jonathan: Will post handoff status in 15m.
lucy: I'll open follow-up ticket for slab defrag + metrics: TASK-4567.
(Last note)
jonathan: Handoff complete. Monitoring stable: p95 ~300-350ms, p99 ~980-1150ms (flapping slightly). Keep watch; escalations only if p99 > 1.5s for 5m.
